mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) compresses equity discount rates and stimulates risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy remains accommodative.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 3.6% signals labor market deterioration and impending corporate earnings contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 3.6% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in industrial production (INDPRO > 110) and labor market strength (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM) indicates robust supply chain capacity utilization, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved earnings visibility.
failure_condition: Both INDPRO > 110 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM occur in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of those instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion regimes defined by high GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized > 2.5%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) typically trigger Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising real rates.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% occurs in 60% of cases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in less than 45% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1600 thousand units signals strong consumer demand and construction activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate sectoral revenue impacts.
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds 1600 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 260 (index) indicates accelerating inflation, prompting Federal Reserve rate hikes that depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains above 260 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 110 indicates robust manufacturing output, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve with sustained capacity utilization.
failure_condition: INDPRO exceeds 110 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Residential sales (RSAFS) exceeding 530,000 million dollars signals strong housing market activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated consumer spending and retail sector momentum.
failure_condition: RSAFS exceeds 530,000 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs. baseline).
